title: ADR: Replayable Inference and Audit-Token Contract
author: Priya Narayanan
body:
Summary:

This ADR defines a company-wide contract for making certain inference requests replayable for audit and debugging while bounding nondeterminism for privacy-sensitive results. It introduces a lightweight audit token that travels with a request and a server-side mode (replayable-mode) that preserves or reconstructs nondeterministic sources where appropriate. The goal is to provide reproducible output for post-hoc investigation while limiting operational cost and privacy surface.

Context and motivation:

- Production inference is increasingly non-deterministic: token sampling, temperature, stochastic decoders, runtime kernel non-determinism (mixed precision / fused kernels), and external tool calls all contribute.
- Customers and internal teams require the ability to replay or re-run a subset of requests to investigate regressions, safety incidents, or billing disputes.
- Full determinism (bit-for-bit) is impractical for most models and hardware configurations; we need a pragmatic contract that provides high-fidelity replay for investigation while respecting privacy, cost, and operational constraints.

Scope:

- Applies to all Redwood-hosted inference endpoints and Dedicated control-plane behaviors.
- Optional support for Private deployments (subject to config toggles in the runtime-sidecar contract).
- Covers text generation and chat endpoints where sampling-based decoding or external tool invocations occur. Does NOT mandate replay for pure deterministic (beam-0, greedy) calls.

Decision (high level):

1) Introduce an "audit_token" (opaque string) that clients may attach to requests when they want guaranteed replayability within a bounded retention window.
2) Define server-side "replayable-mode" semantics: when a request arrives with audit_token and the model/route is eligible, the runtime will:
   - persist a compact replay record (see format below) with configurable TTL;
   - capture determinism-bridging metadata (seed, sampling params, model-variant, quantization profile, kernel versions, host-ABI fingerprint);
   - capture external side effects or tool-call traces needed to reproduce outputs (links to traces, or snapshot of inputs where feasible).
3) Audit-token replay is provided via a privileged API: POST /admin/replay with audit_token + auth; the replay runs under a controlled environment (pinned model artifact, deterministic sampler if available, or replay heuristics) and returns a replay report and candidate outputs.

Audit token and record format (compact):

- audit_token (opaque): 36-char base62 string; created by the control plane when requested (clients may also supply a client-signed token where allowed by customer policy).
- replay_record (stored blob, TTL-configurable):

  - request_id: string
  - client_timestamp: ISO-8601
  - model_artifact: model-id@sha256
  - model_variant: e.g., fp16-qat-v2, int8-q4_0
  - decoder_params: JSON string recording sampling params (temperature, top_p, seed where available)
  - kernel_fingerprint: gpu-driver@ver + runtime-kernel-hash
  - kv_prefix_hash: sha256(prompt-prefix) (to avoid storing PII while enabling matching)
  - external_calls: list of references (trace-ids) or snapshots (if snapshot_enabled)
  - runtime_env: host-image@rev, sidecar-config@rev

Example audit-token creation flow (client):

1. Client sets header X-Request-Audit: need_replay=true in the request or passes top-level param audit_request=true.
2. Control plane returns response header X-Audit-Token: <audit_token> when accepted.
3. Client stores token locally if they plan to request replay later.

Access and governance:

- Replay is a privileged operation and requires authenticated, auditable calls to /admin/replay and RBAC checks. Only owners with "replay:read" may request a replay. All replay attempts are logged with actor and rationale.
- Retention default: 30 days. Configurable per-customer (Enterprise settings) with maximum 365 days under compliance review.

Server behavior and heuristics:

- If runtime can run exactly with seeded RNG and identical kernel path, the replay will set RNG seed and attempt deterministic execution.
- If exact reproduction impossible (different hardware or quantization path), runtime will:
  - first attempt best-effort reconstruction using captured kernel_fingerprint, model_variant, and decoder params;
  - mark the replay as "heuristic_replay" in the report and enumerate differences (kernel mismatch, model artifact diff, missing external calls).
- External tool calls: for HTTP-based tools the replay will either replay recorded snapshots (if snapshotting was enabled) or re-issue calls into a sandbox if customer allows. For privacy-sensitive integrations, only references are stored and replay will be limited to anonymized metadata.

Compatibility and gating rules:

- Not all routes are eligible: routes that explicitly opt-out (by route config: replay_support: false) will not create replay records even if audit token requested. This is important for privacy/regulatory endpoints.
- For high-throughput low-latency routes we default to sampling 1% of requests for replay unless the client explicitly requests persistence (audit header) or the customer tier allows it. Sampling rate is configurable per route.

Configuration table (recommended defaults):

- replay.default_ttl_days: "30" (default retention for replay records)
- replay.max_retention_days: "365" (maximum retention allowed, enterprise opt-in)
- replay.sampling_rate: "0.01" (default fraction of requests to persist when audit header absent)
- replay.snapshot_enabled: "false" (whether to store external-call snapshots by default)
- replay.max_blob_kb: "512" (soft limit on replay_record stored blob size)

API surfaces and examples:

1) Client request example (requesting a replay record):

POST /v1/generate
Headers:
  Authorization: Bearer <token>
  X-Request-Audit: need_replay=true
Body (JSON):
{
  "prompt": "Summarize the quarterly goals.",
  "temperature": 0.7,
  "top_p": 0.9,
  "max_tokens": 256
}

Response headers include: X-Audit-Token: abc123...

2) Admin replay example (privileged):

POST /admin/replay
Headers:
  Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>
Body (JSON):
{
  "audit_token": "abc123...",
  "replay_mode": "pinned-artifact",
  "pin": {
    "model_artifact": "gptx-mini@sha256:...",
    "kernel_version": "v2025-09-03"
  }
}

Response (summary):
{
  "status":"completed",
  "replay_type":"deterministic",
  "differences": ["kernel_mismatch","kv_prefix_truncated"],
  "replay_output_sample": "..."
}

Security and privacy considerations:

- Avoid storing raw prompt text for PII-sensitive tenants. Use prefix hashing (kv_prefix_hash) to enable matching without retaining PII by default.
- Snapshotting of external calls is opt-in and must be encrypted at rest with tenant KMS if enabled for Enterprise customers.
- Audit token issuance is rate-limited and subject to abuse detection; issuance events are logged and alerted on anomalous patterns.

Observability and SLOs for replayability subsystem:

- Metrics to emit: replay_record_ingest_count, replay_record_store_size_bytes, replay_request_latency_ms_p50/p90/p99, replay_success_rate, replay_heuristic_rate.
- Alerting thresholds (examples):
  - replay_request_latency_ms_p99 > 10s for 15m -> P0 to infra team
  - replay_success_rate < 95% for 1h -> P1 to runtime owner
  - replay_store_growth_rate > 2x expected -> cost-control alert to finance

Rollout and migration plan (stepwise):

1. Design and implement minimal control-plane headers and ephemeral audit token generation (no persistent storage) - feature flag off by default.
2. Implement lightweight replay_record schema and local dev-test retention storage; enable for internal tenants only at 0.1% sampling.
3. Expand to selected customers (pilot) with explicit audit header support and 30-day retention; enable snapshotting off.
4. Add admin replay API and RBAC controls; conduct tabletop exercises with security and legal.
5. Harden storage (encryption, KMS per-tenant) and expose Enterprise retention config.
6. Public rollout with documentation, SDK helpers, and runtime metrics.

Testing and acceptance criteria:

- Unit tests for audit token creation, header handling, and replay_record generation.
- End-to-end tests: create audit_token -> persist record -> admin replay returns a replay_report with status.
- Chaos tests: replay under kernel-mismatch simulator should produce heuristic_replay and enumerated differences.

Consequences and trade-offs:

- Pros: provides a practical middle path between no replayability and full determinism; enables faster incident triage and customer dispute resolution.
- Cons: added storage/cost; increased attack surface for sensitive prompts; operational complexity (RBAC, retention policies).

Open questions / future work:

- Standardizing cross-tenant cryptographic proofs that a replay is faithful without exposing prompts (zero-knowledge or HMAC proofs).
- Define formal SLAs for replay turnaround (e.g., 95th percentile replay completion time).
- Extending contract to streaming endpoints with incremental replay checkpoints.

Related pages and references:
